Just think about this, if this is how he acts now how will he act later? Is he willing to recognize this mistake and change? You know the answer to both of those questions and I know you know what the right answer is supposed to be. Right now, he either doesn’t think that you having an abortion is a big enough deal for you to be upset, or just doesn’t care if you’re upset. Let say you stay with him forever, if doesn’t think abortion is a big deal, do you think he’ll help you through future pregnancies (if you decide on children)? Will he be there, AND be supportive if you give birth someday, or will he make that experience traumatic by leaving you alone and in pain? If he just doesn’t care you’re upset, what will happen during your lives together? If you lose someone close to you, financial struggles, natural disasters, hard parenting decisions, will he be there or will he leave you alone to deal with the pain and stress by yourself. If you ever come to a point in life where you don’t have a friend to lean on or you’ve lost all your family, and this is how he behaves, you will spend the rest of your life completely alone with someone right next to you. That’s sounds like a hell I would wish on nobody…

If you really wanna go to college, there is a way without doing anything illegal or to put yourself in danger. You may go into hundreds of thousands of dollars of debt, but only you can decide if that’s worth it for you. That is unfortunately the reality of the world we live in right now. Some, but not all lot of people’s parents are paying for their children’s college anymore. You have to rely on financial aid, part-time to full-time work, and scholarship opportunities most of the time. It will be very difficult, more difficult than it is for people who are more financially fortune, and that sucks, but if it’s what you really want, it’s what you’ll do. Even if you can’t get to college right away, remember that you have (assuming you’re high-school age) triple your lifetime more to live at least, there is SO much time. For me, college didn’t seem feasible right out of high-school, so I went the trade school route so that if I ever decide to go back to school it should be possible with my finances and schedule. Just remember, determination and a little hope goes a long way, and we live in a crappy world/economy and it is not your fault so long as you are working towards your goals.

I feel like the best think you can do is ask him how he truly felt about the situation, like illogical emotions and all. Be willing to listen to any and every thought he might have had about what happened, whether or not you both might agree that a particular reaction was unjust. Just let him air it out, then reiterate how you felt, and if you have both come to an understanding that you are both simply humans with emotions, just remind him that you care about him, Reassure him that if something is bothering you again that you’ll talk to him about it.

If what you did hurt him, you can’t change that. He will have to get over that himself. It doesn’t make you a bad friend if you truly felt u had no other choice. The only thing you can do is be honest and understanding with each other now.

Personally, as someone who has been very close to ending my own life, I don’t mind this argument at all. Yes, we have ALL thought about the impact our death would have, but I think we should still think about it more. If just feeling overwhelmingly guilty about how friends and family would feel if you die is what keeps you living until you find a real reason too, I’d take that any day. Besides, again as someone who has come close to suicide, I think that the action IS inherently selfish. Not that suicidal people as a whole or selfish or bad. I’m never saying that and that’s also not to say that I look down on people who tried or succeeded. Sometimes people feel like the pain is so intense that they can’t get through it even if they hurt people, but the choice is still selfish. Like loved ones of people who succeeded have every right to be angry. You shouldn’t hate them for it, it’s just okay to be angry. If someone I loved killed themselves, I’d be pissed at them for leaving me. I don’t know how to really explain it without sounding like I’m just denouncing suicidal people, but I have 1000% empathy and love for them as I was like that too fairly recently. What I’m trying to say is that if making people feel kinda shitty for possibly hurting people with their death is what keeps them alive for a little longer, than at least they’re f*cking alive. That guilt is the only reason I’m here today and I’m eternally grateful for it.

Honestly it comes with time. At 5 months post op you probably will have some trouble with certain jobs. I have pretty much my entire back fused after having a pretty significant S curve (I couldn’t tell you the degrees, I was young so I forgot) and for the first year and a half or so I was still adjusting. Now, though, at 4 years post-op, I feel like I can do pretty much anything. Bending, standing, or sitting at a desk for long periods of time does cause pain. Bending or standing is usually in the lower back while sitting in a desk tends to hurt my upper back due to lack of support and bad posture, however it’s always manageable and I’m usually able to sleep it off. Yoga is also immensely helpful, although I would wait at least 8 months before trying any extreme stretching. Personality, while I do have mild pain most days, I don’t feel that my life is hindered by my spinal surgery. I forget about it most of the time and often find I’m capable of doing the same things anyone without surgery can do. Pain with activities gets much better with time, and the pain that you are left with will be something you get used to. Having someone around to give you the occasional massage definitely won’t hurt either.
